claims.text: Cast Co-Cr-Fe-Ni multi-principal-element alloys have limited ductility.
The initial Co-Cr-Fe-Ni alloy has a coarse grain size greater than 10 μm.
Microalloying Co-Cr-Fe-Ni with Mo or C tends to produce brittle intermetallic or Laves phases.
Co-Cr-Fe-Ni containing 0.5 at.% C and 4 at.% Mo can be prepared by vacuum arc melting, solution treatment at 1200 °C, and 70% hot rolling.
The proposed composition and processing route will produce grains smaller than 50 nm.
Adding 0.5 at.% C and 4 at.% Mo will stabilize an FCC+HCP dual-phase constitution in Co-Cr-Fe-Ni.
Carbon segregation at grain boundaries reduces interfacial energy and suppresses grain growth.
A metastable FCC matrix can transform to HCP or form twins during deformation, enabling TRIP or TWIP.
Mo remains in solid solution up to 4 at.% in the C-containing Co-Cr-Fe-Ni alloy without forming Mo4C.
The specified C:Mo ratio prevents nucleation of brittle Mo carbides.
Severe plastic deformation drives grain refinement.
FCC-HCP coexistence and TWIP/TRIP deformation enhance strength through dual-phase and deformation-induced strengthening.
The processed alloy will have yield strength greater than 750 MPa.
The processed alloy will have elongation greater than 60%.
The processed alloy will contain no detectable Mo4C or Laves phase.
The same Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Mo alloy without carbon has an FCC+HCP dual-phase structure.
The corresponding non-carbon Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Mo alloys have micrometre-scale coarse grains.
Increasing Mo above 4 at.% causes Mo-carbide precipitation and brittleness.
Exceeding the annealing stability limit causes grain growth above 50 nm or carbide precipitation.
Annealing below approximately 900 °C for short durations avoids Mo4C precipitation.

contradictions.description: The boundary predicts that Mo above 4 at.% should produce Mo4C, but the falsification rule says detection of Mo4C or Laves phase in the 5 at.% Mo alloy would falsify the hypothesis. That observation would instead confirm the stated boundary.

The conditions require annealing below approximately 900 °C for short durations, whereas the proposed experiment anneals at exactly 900 °C for one hour, which is neither clearly below the threshold nor clearly a short-duration treatment.
